frames.narration: A 12-line discount function: a base rate for orders of 100 or more, a member bonus, a coupon bonus, a cap at 20 percent, then a floored discount. Four suites will test it.
Suite one calls the function with three inputs and asserts nothing. The coverage tool reports every one of the 12 lines ran: 100%.
The mutation tool changes the code in 10 small ways, one at a time: a >= to a >, a + to a -, a floor to a ceil. This suite cannot fail on any of them. 0 of 10 mutants are killed.
Suite two adds one assertion per path. Coverage is the same 100%, but now 7 of the 10 mutants are killed. The 3 survivors: the cap comparison, the floor versus ceil, and the SAVE10 amount.
Suite three adds edge cases: exactly 100, 99, 101, the cap, a rounding case. 8 of 10 are killed. Still 100% coverage; the number never moved, but the protection did.
Suite four checks 60 seeded inputs against an independent reference. 9 of 10 mutants are killed. It costs 660 test runs for the mutation pass, against 33 for suite two.

One mutant still survives: the cap check changed from > to >=. When the rate is exactly 20, setting it to 20 changes nothing, so no test can tell. It is an equivalent mutant, and why a score of 100% is not always the goal.
